# HAProxy — custom-context

App on /app context, proxy preserves the same path so the backend sees the original URL unchanged. HAProxy has no location construct, so nothing has to be said about the context path: this scenario mounts the same shared template as root-context.

Proxy URL on `http://localhost:9090`: `/app/`

## Configuration

See [docker-compose.yml](./docker-compose.yml) for service definitions.

HAProxy config (`haproxy/templates/passthrough.cfg`), mounted as
`conf.d/10-vaadin.cfg`:

```haproxy
# Pass everything through untouched: the public URL and the backend URL are the
# same. Shared by two scenarios, because HAProxy has no <Location> / location
# construct — a frontend accepts every path and a backend carries it — so a
# context path needs no rule:
#
#   root-context     app at /,     proxy at /
#   custom-context   app on /app,  proxy preserves the path
#
# Nor does push. An upgrade is relayed on whatever path it arrives on, so there
# is nothing like the Apache and NGINX *-push-location scenarios, which give the
# push paths an upgrade-capable block of their own, to write here.
frontend vaadin-in from vaadin-front
    bind :80
    default_backend vaadin-app

backend vaadin-app from vaadin
    server vaadin vaadin:8080
```

The `global` section, and the two `defaults` sections this file
inherits from, come from the shared
[haproxy-base.cfg](../../haproxy-base.cfg), mounted read-only beside
it as `conf.d/00-base.cfg`. Base and scenario only parse as a pair.
